meta.project: High Horse Society Essay Judging Service

product_overview: The High Horse Society Essay Judging Service is a backend API designed to enforce quality standards on user-submitted essays by validating length, information density, and logical validity. It aims to facilitate meaningful online social interaction by ensuring only well-crafted, substantive essays are accepted and stored, supporting a social platform where thoughtful posts replace noise.
core_goals: Enforce minimum quality standards for essays including length, information density, and logical coherence.
Provide a robust API for submitting, judging, and retrieving essays with concurrency support.
Store accepted essays with versioning in a PostgreSQL database, supporting optimistic concurrency control.
Support contestation and correction workflows for essays based on logical errors and source validity.
Enable fast, scalable judge operations with health check and concurrency management.
key_features: Essay Judging API endpoint (/essay/judge) to validate essays based on length, density, and logical validity with detailed rationale feedback.
Health check endpoint (/health) to monitor service status.
Essay submission endpoint (/essay/submit) to save new essays or versions to a PostgreSQL backend database with version control.
Essay retrieval endpoint (/essay/get) with support for latest or version-specific retrieval.
PostgreSQL integration with configuration via environment variables and local development support including a local database setup.
Rejection of essays that fail any minimum criteria and approval of essays passing all quality checks.
Idempotency key support to prevent duplicate essay judgments.
Support for eventual contestation and retraction features for essays and sources, enabling a quality-driven social feed.
user_flow_summary: User submits an essay JSON via the /essay/judge POST endpoint including title, body, optional sources, and idempotency key.
The service validates the essay for minimum word count (1000 words), information density, and logical validity, returning a detailed JSON with boolean pass/fail and rationales for each category.
If the essay passes, users can submit the essay via /essay/submit to save it into the PostgreSQL database, applying versioning and concurrency control.
Users retrieve essays through /essay/get by specifying essay ID and optionally a version number, receiving the stored essay version or latest by default.
Health of the service can be checked using the /health GET endpoint.
Future workflows include contestation of essays and sources which can modify essay status and user privileges.
validation_criteria: All essays under 1000 words are rejected with appropriate rationale provided in response.
Essays not meeting information density or logical validity criteria must be rejected with clear explanations.
Approved essays are persisted correctly in the PostgreSQL database with versioning and concurrency controls enforced.
Endpoints /health, /essay/judge, /essay/submit, and /essay/get are fully functional and documented in API specs.
Service supports concurrent requests without failure or data corruption.
Idempotency keys prevent duplicate processing of the same essay submission or judging request.
Local development environment can spin up a functional instance including local PostgreSQL database for testing.
Version conflicts during essay submission are managed using optimistic concurrency, allowing correct version increments.
Database stores all derived quality metrics retrievably for each essay version.
System supports potential future contestation, retraction, and token management features as per the High Horse Society vision.
